concept.title: Rung Budget for Plateau Identification
concept.concept_description:
Exact identifiability shows one rung plus a ratio bound leaves an interval of length d0 r/(1-r) of admissible plateaus. Conjecture that each additional measured rung contracts this interval by exactly the factor r, giving a closed formula for the number of extra rungs needed to identify the plateau to within the U108 CI half-width. This converts 'measure more rungs' into a costed experimental plan.

After m further rungs the admissible plateau interval has length d0 r^{m+1}/(1-r), so identification to within 0.0445 needs ceil(log(0.0445 (1-r)/(d0 r))/log r) rungs, i.e. three at r = 1/2 and d0 = 0.0259.

Generalise plateau_set_exact to a prefix of m measured rungs and compute the resulting interval length in Lean.

The programme has an explicit stopping rule for the bitlen ladder.

Plateau identification is either cheaper or impossible, and the ladder design must change.
